title: Your 2024-25 Smart Classroom Management Report Card port-card/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: This piece presents Linsin's annual self-assessment tool, a 15-item checklist covering behaviors like consistently following the classroom management plan, enforcing consequences calmly like a referee, avoiding all forms of intimidation, and eschewing external rewards in favor of intrinsic motivation. His central claim is that most teachers benefit from a structured, honest self-rating exercise (1-5 per item) that converts into a total score, which he maps onto a martial-arts-style belt rank ranging from white belt (15-30) up through a newly added red belt (70-75). He explains the red-belt tier was added specifically because black belt, while already excellent, still leaves a meaningful gap before reaching what he describes as a nearly "supernatural" level of classroom control and virtuosity. The exercise itself is framed as quick — just a few minutes — but valuable precisely because it forces specific, itemized self-honesty rather than a vague sense of how the year went. The concrete recommendation for anyone scoring low on a given item is to revisit the relevant category in the SCM archive or one of Linsin's books to target that specific weakness.
points: The 15-item scale rates specific behaviors — like calm, referee-style enforcement and avoiding external rewards — on a 1-5 basis.
Scores convert into a martial-arts-style rank running from white belt (15-30) through the newly introduced red belt (70-75).
Red belt was added because black belt, while excellent, still leaves a meaningful performance gap at the very top.
The exercise is designed to be quick but is valued for forcing itemized, specific self-honesty rather than a vague year-end impression.
quotes: The purpose is to assess the extent you were able to follow the principles of Smart Classroom Management.
Because it provides a clear picture of where you need to improve.
If you wish, you can add up your final numbers to earn an SCM belt rank.
However, I added the rank of red belt because it represents a jump in performance to a level of control and virtuosity that can feel as if you’re conducting the New York Philharmonic.
In other words, whatever classroom management excellence you can imagine, you’re able to make happen right in front of you.
The key is to start strong from the very first day of school.
